name: Rafael Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What fills a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead percussion for a theatre band, teach rhythm at a youth centre and record drum parts for local films. I have a music master's and can bring a loose ensemble together, though I still carry my own cases after a late show.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is happening at home around those nights?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Mira works at a clinic, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We have five months of expenses saved, my music pay is fairly typical and a few other venues are nearby. I use AI every day for take labels and draft schedules, then check them against the recording and signed calls.

say: I'd welcome **tidy take labels** while keeping live listening central.
I'd tell players the **quiet ending** still needs the band.
think: Our **five-month reserve** and clinic wage can cover one late film payment.
I use **AI daily** for labels but listen before sending any take.
do: Confirm **signed winter calls** and six paid pupils this week.
Save **seventy** from a cleared film invoice after players and childcare are paid.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about irregular invoices, with enough savings for one delay.
S0.quote: A take labelled 'good' can still have a missed entrance.
fieldNote: His **typical pay** and five-month reserve buffer a delayed film invoice.
His **daily AI labels** still receive an ear check before clients hear a take.

steps.text: Confirm signed winter theatre calls and six paid youth-centre pupils

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the theatre band that tidy recording labels save time, but the cue still comes from us listening to the actors. A quick file name does not play a quiet ending.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A plateau would leave my theatre, teaching and film work much as they are. Five months saved and Mira's clinic wage can carry a late film fee, though the mortgage keeps me careful with dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll confirm the theatre's signed winter calls and my six paid youth-centre pupils for next term. When the next film invoice clears, I'll move seventy into our house reserve after players and childcare are paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about uneven invoices but safe through one delay. A little faster administration would not take the sticks from my hands.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened after the late film invoice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A producer paid two weeks late in August. Mira's pay covered food and my pupils covered the mortgage, so we did not use the reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you check an automatic take label?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use AI to label takes, but I listen to each one before sending the file. A take labelled 'good' can still have a missed entrance.

say: I'd ask for **paid edit hours** before the studio changes its contract.
I'd bring **ten invoices** to the musicians association.
think: Nearly **one-third of my pay** from edits and planning could shrink.
A **five-month reserve** cannot replace that recurring income.
do: Compare **ten invoices** with offers and bring them to the association this month.
Learn the new **AI separation tool** only in paid instruction on owned takes with licence and approved local storage.
Check **every split** against original; require written permission and stop for invented/missing parts or studio-storage failure.
feel: I feel **anxious** because paid editing may shrink despite an easier workflow.
S1.quote: A faster drum edit is useful only if an editing fee still reaches my invoice.
fieldNote: His **editing and planning fees** make up a third of income at risk.
His **new tool trial** requires paid instruction, owned takes, paid-use licence, local storage, manual checks and consent.

steps.text: Bring ten editing invoices and new offers to musicians association
Train in paid studio session on owned takes with licensed local storage
Compare splits with original; stop for invented hits, missing parts or studio-storage breach
Require written player or family permission before other recordings enter tool

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the theatre and studio which paid edit and booking hours software removes. I would bring recent invoices to the musicians association before the next contract is set.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Editing drum takes and planning rehearsals are nearly a third of my pay. Clients may stop buying those hours while still asking me to play, and five months saved will not replace a lasting third-pay loss.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare ten editing invoices with the new offers and take them to the association. In the first year of change, I'll learn a new AI drum-separation tool, which splits a recording into individual instrument tracks, in a paid studio session, testing only my own raw takes if its licence permits paid work and local storage is approved; I'll compare every split with the original and stop if it invents hits or sends a file outside the studio.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about fewer paid hours, even if the editing gets easier. A faster drum edit is useful only if an editing fee still reaches my invoice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Whose take can go into the new tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will not put another player's take or a pupil recording into the tool without written permission. A missing cymbal or a false snare hit sends me back to the original recording.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the association to seek?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The association can ask for a minimum paid edit and a limit on free drafts. I will bring the ten invoices so the request is based on work we actually sold.

say: I'd seek **signed live dates** before AGI changes paid editing.
I'd tell players **robot drummers** follow thinking AGI by about three years.
think: **AGI in 2028** could remove edits before robot players arrive around 2031.
Our **five-month reserve** supports a search but not a lasting fee gap.
do: List **three income streams** and request signed venue dates now.
Apply **after 2028** if edits halve, only for a posted trainee role with accepted skills, childcare and written replacement net pay.
Keep **current theatre and pupils** until offer; ask lender about full interest before arrears if nights fall.
feel: I feel **anxious** about fee loss, with savings and some local venues giving control.
S2.quote: A manager's friendly word is not a shift on the payroll.
fieldNote: His **2028 screen-fee loss** precedes robot drumming around 2031.
His **trainee application** needs a posted vacancy, accepted degree or skills test, childcare and written net pay after travel.

steps.text: Keep theatre/pupils until signed offer; list income and request signed next-season calls
Apply after 2028 if edits halve and posted trainee accepts degree or test
Require childcare and written net pay after travel replacing fees before leaving theatre or pupils

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the band that AGI by 2028 could edit our recordings before robots can play drums around 2031. I would ask for the next season's paid live dates in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The editing and planning part could become cheap at once, while a theatre still needs a drummer for the show. If those fees halve, five months saved helps us search, but our mortgage still needs a monthly wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll list studio, theatre and lesson pay and request signed paid venue dates. In the first year after 2028, if editing fees halve, I'll apply for a posted live-sound trainee post only if the venue accepts my master's or skills test, childcare fits and written net pay after travel replaces lost fees. I'll keep current theatre and pupils until another offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a real income loss, but two nearby venues give me leads to ask about. A manager's friendly word is not a shift on the payroll.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is a live-sound trainee post open now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One venue filled a trainee role last winter. I'll ask when another is advertised, but I cannot put an old posting in the household budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the theatre also cuts a night?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the theatre also cuts a paid night, Mira and I would ask our lender about temporary terms before arrears. We will compare the total added interest before signing.

say: I'd ask for a **funded sound course** accepted by local venues.
I'd seek **posted paid sound shifts**, not rely on a certificate alone.
think: **AGI in 2031** may remove edits before stage robots arrive around 2034.
**Ordinary software** may reduce paid editing during the warning years.
do: Ask the **college** about grant, accepted certificate and pickup-compatible classes next term.

Seek **posted sound work** after 2031 only if edits fall, certificate qualifies, written net pay improves budget and pickup fits.
feel: I feel **anxious** because editing income may fall while training takes paid time.
S3.quote: A certificate alone does not schedule a paid shift.
fieldNote: His **five-year plan** needs grant funding, venue acceptance, college equipment and childcare-compatible classes.
His **job move** needs a real posted shift, qualifying certificate, written net pay after travel and existing paid work until offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the youth centre five years could let us train people to run a room safely. I would ask the technical college what its live-sound course costs and which venues accept it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2031 may take edits and rehearsal plans, while robots handling stage gear follow around 2034. Ordinary software may cheapen edit work sooner, so I need a paid skill that works in a real venue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next term I'll ask the college whether a grant covers its live-sound course, nearby venues accept the certificate and classes fit Mira's clinic rota for child pickup. I'll enrol only if all three are confirmed and I can use the college's practice desk rather than buy gear. In the first year after AGI, if edit income falls, I'll seek a posted paid sound shift only if the certificate qualifies me, its written net pay after travel improves our budget and pickup still works; I'll keep theatre and pupils until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because training time and mortgage payments happen together. I can learn a new room. A certificate alone does not schedule a paid shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy equipment or childcare for the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The college has a practice desk and microphones. If the next class clashes with Mira's late shift, I will wait for a later intake instead of spending our reserve on childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Has a venue offered a paid sound shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The venue manager mentioned possible work but posted nothing. I would ask for an actual paid vacancy and rate in writing before changing the theatre calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the theatre players a decade is enough to build a paid local percussion night, if the numbers work. I would put player rates in writing before printing a poster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 in 2036 I still need a wage, and robot drummers could reach stages around 2039. Edit fees may thin long before then, so a live series must earn its way without eating the mortgage reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll ask the town hall about a monthly percussion evening only if a sponsor clears room and insurance costs, the hall signs its terms and twelve tickets are prepaid to cover written player rates. By 2036 I'll aim for six months of expenses by saving eighty from each cleared extra teaching fee after players, childcare and the mortgage are paid; in the first year after AGI, I'll continue the evening only if the sponsor renews, hall insurance remains written and twelve tickets still cover the players.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about edit clients leaving before a decade passes. I can test a concert, but I will not use the family's reserve to make a thin audience look full.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must happen before the poster, and if only eight tickets sell?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Before any poster goes up, sponsor money must clear and the hall must put insurance in writing. Players will see and accept their rate first; if only eight tickets sell, I will refund the eight buyers and keep my teaching dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could a pupil recording advertise the evening?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will not use a pupil's practice recording to advertise the night without written family permission. The evening can begin with a live demonstration instead.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because paid edits could halve before a venue offers another wage. Signed theatre dates, a real qualified trainee opening and full lender costs if live nights also fall would help us plan.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who signs off before a recorded drum take is used again. A separated drum track is not a fair deal until the recorded player agrees to its reuse in writing.

headlineQuote: A separated drum track is not a fair deal until the recorded player agrees to its reuse in writing.
portrait: Rafael is a **43-year-old percussion lead** with a music master's, partner, two children and a mortgage.
His **typical pay** and five-month reserve buffer delays, but editing and planning supply a third of income.
He uses **AI daily** and trials new separation only with paid instruction, local storage, listening checks and written consent.
He pursues **funded sound training** and a covered live series while keeping paid theatre work until another offer.
biggestWorry: He fears **AGI by 2028** could halve edits before another paid venue role appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed theatre dates**, a posted qualifying trainee role and full lender costs would help the household plan.
